blocks.md: This lesson follows **Historical Perspective and Further Reading** in *Introduction* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Introduction, § Historical Perspective and Further Reading
blocks.md: The closed-loop architecture at the core of agentic systems predates modern machine learning by decades. In founding cybernetics, Norbert Wiener established feedback as the organizing principle of control, in which a system observes its environment, measures the discrepancy between current state and a target goal, and applies corrective actions. Writing a decade later, Wiener warned of the operational hazard inherent in rapid feedback, arguing that when an automated machine acts faster than a human operator can intervene, it must be constrained to the exact purpose intended.

Every side effect passes an explicit runtime-checked grant and evidence comes only from tools and deterministic checks, never from model text.

The repair, research, remediation, and support agents each bind on a different constraint (compounding and resend, untrusted input and fan-out, blast radius and approval latency, tail latency and session state) and recur as the volume's running cases.

The ordered record of states, proposals, runtime decisions, and observations from initial context to acceptance, termination, or escalation is the accounting boundary for cost, latency, state lifetime, quotas, and permissions, so resources are managed per task rather than per call.
